title: FOOTBALL | Sanfrisco Magee Press Conference - 11/22/26
text: Chris got a couple. You're a guy that grew up in Mississippi, obviously, and at one point you were committed to Old Miss and you flipped to Mississippi State. So, kind of give us your thoughts on the rivalry. >> Um, the rivalry is, um, it's a great rivalry. It's one of the best rivalries that's around here. And, um, growing up, I really ain't watched the rivalry, so I don't know too much about it, but like I just know it's a big um, and hard rivalry. People go at it hard. >> A lot of people kind of waiting to hear uh, kind of what what your plans are, you know, for next season. and beyond. Maybe kind of tell us where you are in that process. >> Oh, right now I'm just trying to go one week at a time, like go one and0 every week. >> Obviously, it's been hard for this offense in general to generate explosive plays since September, but this miss offense is pretty susceptible to those things. Just what do you feel like it's going to take for this offense and to be able to take advantage of the opportunities Miss gives you to make big plays and what's it going to take for you individually to help to contribute to that effort? We just got to make the layups and like do everything that we taught in practice and like don't try to be too greedy. Just take what they give us and like >> saw aunt sort of break through yesterday after kind of weeks of frustration from him. Just, you know, what was it like watching him break through against Tennessee Tech yesterday? >> Um it felt good. Um I think he kind of got kind of uplifted like I I think he could do it more. Um, next week he going to try, we going to try to get him to break the record. Hopefully hopefully he can break it. Yeah. >> Frisco, you're leading the receiving core and receiving touchdowns this year. Uh, kind of talk about your ability to get in the end zone and your knack to score. >> Well, I guess I just a touchdown make when the ball get in my hand, I'm only going one way. That's touchdown. >> You've had to play with four different quarterbacks this year. And like Leb said, the call sheet now is different than it was in September. H how difficult an adjustment has that been kind of getting used to kind of a new offense in many respects, but also different quarterbacks and different playing styles. >> Really the quarterback don't matter. Whoever in we going to execute the plays he throw. We got to be able to get it and like really the quarterback situation just don't matter. Like you just got to make the plays and like be there where you supposed to be at. >> When you look back start of the season and see how you've played through the course. How have you gotten better? And you kind of say, are you surprised that you've made this much progress this year? >> Yeah, I am very surprised. Like for before the season, I set myself a goal and I like exceeded the goal from what I wrote on the paper with my coach. So like, yeah, after the season, I'm going to look at it and I'm like, whoa, I beat it my goal. >> You said you want to help uh a get that record even if it means giving up a catch yourself. >> Nah. No, I can't I can't get in one of my kitchens cuz I barely get some. But like Yeah. >> Got two for you. Number the first order of business. Um can you feel the a different type of intensity in the locker room heading into a game like this versus, you know, the other games? >> Um no, we really just the same every week. It's the same goal, same mindset. Go one and0 every week and um get postseason eligibility. And second one, I don't know if anyone's ever asked you this, but you do a lot you do the same touchdown celebration. You've scored a lot of touchdowns this year. What's the What is that and what what's the story behind it? >> Um, so it's really like some Louisiana type of dance thingy. And like since I did the first game, people told me don't I was going to change it up, but people told me don't change it up. Just like keep it the same and people started doing it. Little kids started doing it and yeah, I just kept it the same. Steve, >> uh, we've never experienced this, but you know, when the ball's in the air and it's you and a DB one-on-one out there and I mean, I don't know if you hear the crowd at all, but what's that moment like and what goes through your mind to ensure that you make the catch rather than him break the pass up? >> Um, really every time the ball go, it's really 955 with the DB with me. So, like if the ball up in there, I'm going try to make the play. I got to make the play cuz like we ain't been getting no really explosive plays. So, we got to get the ones that we can make. >> Do you hear the crowd or you just block? >> No, I just be locked in on the ball. Like zoomed in on the ball. >> Anything else? >> No, he have no name. >> Thanks, guys. >> Thank you.
